learningObjectives.title: The creation of Israel and early Arab-Israeli wars

questions.q: In which month and year did David Ben-Gurion declare the establishment of the State of Israel?
options: May 1948
November 1947
June 1967
October 1973
questions.explain: Israel declared its independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate ended.

questions.q: In which year did the Balfour Declaration express British support for a Jewish national home in Palestine?
questions.explain: The Balfour Declaration was issued in November 1917 during the First World War.

questions.q: When did the United Nations vote to partition Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states (Resolution 181)?
options: November 1947
May 1948
July 1956
June 1967
questions.explain: The UN approved the partition plan on 29 November 1947, dividing Palestine into Jewish and Arab states.

questions.q: Why did Palestinian Arabs and neighbouring Arab states reject the 1947 UN partition plan?
options: It gave the Jewish population, then a minority, a larger share of the land
It placed all of Jerusalem under permanent Jewish control
It required Arab states to pay reparations to Israel
It banned Arabs from owning any land in Palestine
questions.explain: Arabs saw the plan as unjust because Jews, then about a third of the population, were allocated the majority of the territory.

questions.q: Which country governed Palestine under a mandate before 1948?
options: Britain
France
The United States
Turkey
questions.explain: Britain held the Mandate for Palestine from after the First World War until 1948.

questions.q: What does the Arabic term 'Nakba' ('catastrophe') refer to?
options: The displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinian Arabs during the 1948 war
Israel's early defeats in the 1973 war
The nationalisation of the Suez Canal by Nasser
The assassination of Yitzhak Rabin in 1995
questions.explain: The Nakba refers to the flight and expulsion of around 700,000 Palestinians during the 1948-49 war.

questions.q: Why did President Nasser's nationalisation of the Suez Canal in 1956 lead to an international crisis?
options: Britain, France and Israel launched a military attack to regain control of the canal
The USA invaded Egypt to protect Israel's borders
The Soviet Union seized the canal for itself
Egypt declared war on Saudi Arabia over the canal
questions.explain: The strategically vital canal's nationalisation prompted a British, French and Israeli attack on Egypt in the 1956 Suez Crisis.

questions.q: A Palestinian family forced to flee their home during the 1948 war would most likely have become which of the following?
options: Refugees in neighbouring Arab states or in the West Bank and Gaza
Citizens of a new independent Palestinian state
Members of the Israeli parliament
Settlers in the Golan Heights
questions.explain: The 1948 war created a large Palestinian refugee population that fled to surrounding Arab-held areas and states.

questions.q: In which year did the Six-Day War take place?
questions.explain: The Six-Day War was fought between Israel and its Arab neighbours in June 1967.

questions.q: Why was Israel's capture of East Jerusalem and the West Bank in 1967 especially significant?
options: It placed a large Palestinian population and major religious sites under Israeli occupation
It gave Egypt control of the Sinai Peninsula
It ended all conflict in the region permanently
It forced Israel to give up the city of Tel Aviv
questions.explain: Occupying these areas brought over a million Palestinians and contested holy sites under Israeli control, fuelling long-term tension.

questions.q: Israel destroyed most of Egypt's air force on the ground on the first morning of the 1967 war. This best explains why the war...
options: Was won by Israel within six days as it gained control of the skies
Lasted for over a year of fighting
Ended with Egypt capturing Tel Aviv
Led to Soviet troops joining the fighting
questions.explain: The pre-emptive strike gave Israel air superiority, allowing a rapid victory in just six days.

questions.q: What did UN Resolution 242, passed after the 1967 war, principally call for?
options: Israeli withdrawal from occupied territories in exchange for peace
The immediate creation of an independent Palestinian state
The expulsion of Israel from the United Nations
A permanent Arab oil embargo on the West
questions.explain: Resolution 242 established the 'land for peace' principle that shaped later negotiations.

questions.q: Why did Egypt and Syria's timing of the 1973 attack give them an early advantage over Israel?
options: They attacked by surprise on the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur
They had developed nuclear weapons
Israel's army was fighting a war in Lebanon
The USA had refused to supply Israel with any weapons
questions.explain: Launching the assault on Yom Kippur caught a less-prepared Israel by surprise in October 1973.

questions.q: Why did the 1973 war have a major impact beyond the Middle East?
options: Arab oil-producing states raised prices and cut supply, causing a global oil crisis
Israel bombed several European cities
The Suez Canal was permanently closed to all shipping
The United Nations was dissolved as a result
questions.explain: Arab OPEC states used oil as a weapon, triggering a worldwide energy crisis and higher prices.

questions.q: A historian notes that after 1967 Israel governed over a million Palestinians in the occupied territories. This best helps explain the causes of which later event?
options: The First Intifada of 1987
The Balfour Declaration
The 1956 Suez Crisis
The 1948 war of independence
questions.explain: Frustration under prolonged occupation was a key cause of the Palestinian uprising, the First Intifada, in 1987.

questions.q: What was the main significance of the 1978 Camp David Accords?
options: They created the framework for a peace agreement between Israel and Egypt
They established an independent Palestinian state
They brought the Cold War to an end
They handed the Golan Heights back to Syria
questions.explain: Brokered by US President Carter, the accords led to the first peace treaty between Israel and an Arab state.

questions.q: The 1979 peace treaty made Egypt the first Arab state to do what?
options: Officially recognise the State of Israel
Join the United Nations
Capture the Golan Heights
Lead the PLO
questions.explain: The 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty made Egypt the first Arab state to formally recognise Israel.

questions.q: Why was President Sadat of Egypt assassinated in 1981?
options: Islamist militants opposed his peace treaty with Israel
He had lost the 1973 war against Israel
He refused to nationalise the Suez Canal
He had signed the Oslo Accords
questions.explain: Sadat was killed by Islamist extremists angered by his 1979 peace with Israel.

questions.q: The Oslo Accords, signed in 1993, were an agreement between Israel and which organisation?
options: The PLO
OPEC
The Arab League
Hamas
questions.explain: The 1993 Oslo Accords involved mutual recognition between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).

questions.q: Yitzhak Rabin was assassinated in 1995 by a right-wing Israeli opposed to the Oslo peace process. What does this best suggest about peace-making in this period?
options: Opposition to a negotiated peace existed within Israel itself, not only among Arabs
All Israelis fully supported the Oslo Accords
Only Arab states ever opposed the peace process
The peace process faced no serious resistance
questions.explain: Rabin's murder by an Israeli extremist shows that resistance to compromise came from within Israel as well as from Arab opponents.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History (1HI0) specification; Conflict in the Middle East 1945-95
